description: LLBwithMe question bank — complete curriculum structure for all semesters. Each subject's questions live in data/questions/<subject_id>.json. This file is the single source of truth for semester, subject, and module metadata.

semesters.name: Semester 1
semesters.description: Foundation courses covering criminal psychology, constitutional law, contract law, family law, law of crimes, and intellectual property rights.

subjects.name: Criminal Psychology & Criminal Sociology
subjects.description: Study of criminal behavior, criminological theories, psychological approaches to crime, and sociological perspectives on criminal conduct.

modules.name: Sociological Theories - Crime and Social Structure

subjects.name: Constitutional Law I
subjects.description: Fundamental principles of the Indian Constitution, Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles, and constitutional interpretation.

modules.name: Territory of India, Citizenship & General Principles Relating to Fundamental Rights (Articles 12 and 13)
Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25 to 28) and Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29 to 30)
Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36 to 51) and Fundamental Duties (Article 51A)
Out of Syllabus
modules.description: Questions that appear in examination papers but cover topics outside the defined syllabus scope for this subject. Retained for reference.

subjects.name: Law of Contract I
subjects.description: Formation, validity, performance, and discharge of contracts under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 and Specific Relief Act, 1963.

modules.name: Out of Syllabus
modules.description: Questions that appear in examination papers but cover topics outside the defined syllabus scope for this subject. Retained for reference.

subjects.name: Family Law I
subjects.description: Personal laws governing marriage, divorce, adoption, and maintenance across Hindu, Muslim, Christian, and Parsi communities.

modules.name: Introduction to Hindu and Muslim Law
Marriage and Matrimonial Reliefs under Hindu Law
Marriage and Matrimonial Reliefs under Muslim Law
Out of Syllabus
modules.description: Questions that appear in examination papers but cover topics outside the defined syllabus scope for this subject. Retained for reference.

subjects.name: Law of Crimes
subjects.description: Study of criminal offences, liability, punishments, and defenses under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS).

modules.name: Out of Syllabus
modules.description: Questions that appear in examination papers but cover topics outside the defined syllabus scope for this subject. Retained for reference.

subjects.name: Intellectual Property Rights
subjects.description: Legal framework for protection of patents, copyrights, trademarks, designs, and geographical indications.

semesters.name: Semester 2
semesters.description: Advanced legal studies covering Constitutional Law II, Contract Law II, Family Law II, Penology & Victimology, Jurisprudence, and Media Law.

subjects.name: Constitutional Law II
subjects.description: Federal structure of India, distribution of legislative and executive powers, Union and State legislatures, emergency provisions, constitutional bodies, and the Basic Structure Doctrine.

modules.name: Nature of Indian Federalism
modules.description: Essential characteristics of Indian Federalism, comparison with American Federalism, and the relationship between Federalism and the Basic Structure Doctrine.
topics: Essential characteristics of Indian Federalism
Indian Federalism distinguished from American Federalism
Federalism and Basic Structure Doctrine

modules.name: Distribution of Legislative and Executive Powers
modules.description: The scheme of distribution of legislative powers, territorial extent, limitations on Parliament, legislative subjects, residuary powers, expansion of Union powers, interpretation of lists, executive powers, Centre-State coordination, and inter-governmental delegation.
topics: The Scheme of Distribution of Legislative powers
Territorial extent of Union and State Legislature
Limitations to the territorial jurisdiction of the Parliament
Distribution of Legislative subjects
Residuary powers
Expansion of Legislative powers of the Union under different circumstances
Interpretation of Legislative lists
Distribution of Executive powers
Centre-State Co-ordination
Inter-Governmental Delegation of Powers
Delegation by the Centre
Entrustment of State's Power to the Centre
Centre's direction to the State
All India Services
Inter-State Council

modules.name: Distribution of Financial Powers
modules.description: Allocation of taxing powers, restrictions on States' taxing powers, distribution of revenue between Union and States, and grant-in-aid.
topics: Allocation of Taxing Powers
Restriction of State's Power to levy Taxes
Distribution of Revenue between the Union and the States
Assignment of Union Revenue to the State
Compulsory Tax Sharing
Permissive Sharing of Taxes
Grant-in-Aid

modules.name: Structure, Powers and Functions of Union and State Legislature
modules.description: Bicameral legislature, composition/powers/functions of Parliament and State Legislatures, qualifications/disqualifications/privileges of members, anti-defection law, and law-making procedure including types of bills.
topics: Bicameral Legislature
Composition, Powers and Functions of Union Legislature
Composition, Powers and Functions of State Legislature
Qualification, Disqualification and Privileges of Members of Parliament
Members of Legislative Assembly
Anti-Defection Law
Law making procedure — Types of Bills: Ordinary, Financial, Money, Appropriation, Private Member Bills, Government/Public Bills

modules.name: Structure, Powers and Functions of Supreme Court, High Court and Tribunals
modules.description: Judicial independence, appointment of judges, structure, jurisdiction, powers and functions of the Supreme Court, High Courts and Subordinate Courts, Tribunals, and judicial accountability.
topics: Independence of Judiciary and Judicial Activism
Appointment of Judges, Structure, Jurisdiction, Power and Functions of Supreme Court
Appointment of Judges, Structure, Jurisdiction, Power and Functions of High Court and Subordinate Courts
Tribunals — Administrative tribunals, Tribunals for other matters
Judicial accountability and demand of National Judicial Appointments Commission

modules.name: Structure, Powers and Functions of Union and State Executive
modules.description: Union Executive — President, Vice-President, Council of Ministers. State Executive — Governor, State Council of Ministers. Interaction between executive and legislature, and conduct of government business.
topics: Union Executive — Appointment, Qualification, Powers and Functions of President and Vice-President, Union Council of Ministers
State Executive — Appointment, Qualification, Powers and Functions of Governor, State Council of Ministers
Interaction between the Executives and the Legislature
Conduct of Government Business

modules.name: Other Constitutional Institutions / Authorities
modules.description: UPSC, Attorney General, Election Commission, CAG, Local Self-Governing Bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities), and National Commissions for SC/ST/Backward Classes.
topics: UPSC and State Public Service Commission
Attorney General, Advocate General
Election Commission of India
Comptroller and Auditor General of India
Local Self-Governing Bodies: Panchayats and Municipalities, Co-operative Societies
National Commissions for SC, ST and Backward Classes

modules.name: Emergency Provisions
modules.description: National Emergency, failure of constitutional machinery in a State, and Financial Emergency.
topics: National Emergency
Failure of Constitutional Machinery in a State
Financial Emergency

modules.name: Out of Syllabus
modules.description: Questions from exam papers that fall outside the defined SPPU syllabus scope.

subjects.name: Law of Contract II
subjects.description: Special contracts under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Indemnity (Ss.124-125), Guarantee (Ss.126-147), and Bailment (Ss.148-171). Examination papers also cover Agency, Sale of Goods, and Partnership.

modules.name: Contracts of Indemnity
modules.description: Contracts of Indemnity under Sections 124-125 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
topics: Principle of indemnity in general
Meaning and definition of the contract of indemnity
Formation and essential features
Nature and extent of liability of the indemnifier
Commencement of liability of the indemnifier
Examples: duplicate share certificate; bank deposit receipt; local authority commencement certificate; publisher-printer clause; sale deed assurance of title

modules.name: Contracts of Guarantee
modules.description: Contracts of Guarantee under Sections 126-147 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
topics: Definition of a contract of guarantee and kinds of guarantee
Formation, essential features and parties
Contract of guarantee distinguished from indemnity
Consideration for a contract of guarantee
Continuing guarantee and its revocation
Nature and extent of surety's liability — commencement, duration, termination and discharge
Surety's rights against the principal debtor
Surety's rights against the creditor
Letters of credit and bank guarantees
Co-surety and manner of sharing liabilities and rights

modules.name: Contracts of Bailment
modules.description: Contracts of Bailment under Sections 71, 148-171, 180-181 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
topics: Definition of a contract of Bailment
Formation, essential features and parties
Kinds of Bailment
Examples: for benefit of bailor, for benefit of bailee
Rights, duties, disabilities and liabilities of bailor and bailee vis-à-vis third parties and true owner
Termination of bailment and consequences
Finder of goods as a bailee

modules.name: Contracts of Pledge
modules.description: Contracts of Pledge under Sections 172-179 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
topics: Meaning and definition of a contract of Pledge
Essential features and parties
Creation of a contract of pledge
Distinction between pledge, bailment and hypothecation
Rights, liabilities, duties and disabilities of the pawnor
Rights, liabilities, duties and disabilities of the pawnee
Pledge by certain specified persons: Sections 178, 178A, 179 of ICA

modules.name: Contracts of Agency
modules.description: Contracts of Agency under Sections 182-238 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
topics: Meaning and definition of a contract of Agency
Essential features; parties; kinds of agents and agencies
Creation of agency
Distinction between agent, servant/employee, and independent contractor
Agent's authority — express, implied, apparent/ostensible, emergency, restrictions
Delegation of authority; principal, agent, sub-agent and substituted agents
Rights, duties, immunities, disabilities and liabilities of an agent
Rights, duties, immunities, disabilities and liabilities of a principal
Personal liability of agent; Pretended agent; Undisclosed principal
Revocation and other modes of termination; Irrevocable agency; Effect of termination

modules.name: Contracts of Sale of Goods
modules.description: The Sale of Goods Act, 1930.
topics: Definition of a contract of Sale of Goods
Essential features; parties, goods, price, delivery, risk and property
Sale as transfer of property; sale and agreement to sell; effect of perishing of goods
Goods — meaning, existing and future, specific, ascertained, unascertained and contingent
Implied and express conditions and warranties
The rule of caveat emptor and exceptions
Transfer of title; Nemo Dat Quod Non Habet and passing of risk
Rules as to delivery; modes of delivery; inspection and rejection of goods
Rights and liabilities of buyer and seller; Unpaid seller and his rights
Remedies for price and breach; interest and taxes
Auction sales

modules.name: Contracts of Partnership
modules.description: The Indian Partnership Act, 1932 and The Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.
topics: Meaning and definition of a contract of partnership
Essential features; firm; firm name; business; property; Minor as a partner
Kinds of partnership
Relations of partners inter se — rights, liabilities, duties, immunities, disabilities
Relations of partners to third parties; partner as agent of firm; liability for acts of partners
Change in constitution of firm; admission, retirement, expulsion, death, insolvency
Dissolution of a firm — modes, effect, agreements in restraint of trade
Registration of firms — procedure and effect of non-registration
Limited Liability Partnership — essential features; distinction from ordinary partnership

subjects.name: Family Law II
subjects.description: Hindu Joint Family System, coparcenary, Karta, partition, and intestate succession under HSA 1956, Muslim law, and the Indian Succession Act 1925.

modules.name: Hindu Joint Family System
modules.description: Evolution and institution of the Hindu joint family, coparcenary under Mitakshara and Dayabhaga, Karta's position and powers, alienation of coparcenary property, and partition.
topics: Evolution of joint family system in India
Institution of Hindu joint family and joint family property; family arrangement; separate or self-acquired property
Coparcenary, Mitakshara and Dayabhaga coparcenary; Women as coparceners; Rights and powers of coparceners; sole surviving coparcener; Effect of amendments to HSA 1956
Karta — position, powers and duties; Father's powers of alienation; Alienee's rights and remedies
Partition — under Dayabhaga and Mitakshara systems; subject matter; persons entitled; kinds of partition; principle of survivorship and representation; Reopening and Reunion

modules.name: Intestate Succession
modules.description: Rules of intestate succession under the Hindu Succession Act 1956, Muslim law (Sunni and Shia), and the Indian Succession Act 1925 (Parsis, Christians, domicile).
topics: Hindu Succession Act 1956 — Application of Act; succession to property of Hindu male; succession to property of Hindu female; stridhana and women's estate; general provisions; disqualifications from inheritance; Escheat
General principles of inheritance under Muslim law; law applicable to Sunnis and Shias; distinction between the two; disqualifications

Indian Succession Act 1925 — Domicile and its relevance in succession; consanguinity; intestate succession applicable to Parsis and persons other than Parsis; general principles of succession; rules of devolution

modules.name: Testamentary Succession
modules.description: Wills and codicils under the Indian Succession Act 1925, Hindu testamentary succession, and Wasiyat (will under Muslim law).
topics: Indian Succession Act 1925 — Wills and codicils; competence of testator; execution of privileged and unprivileged will; attestation; revocation, alteration and revival; construction of wills
Indian Succession Act 1925 — Vesting of legacies; void, onerous, contingent and conditional bequests; specific and demonstrative legacies; ademption; lapse; election; gifts in contemplation of death
Hindu Succession Act 1956 — Testamentary succession
Will under Muslim law (Wasiyat)

modules.name: Right of Pre-emption
modules.description: Pre-emption under Muslim law (Shufa) and under Hindu law.
topics: Pre-emption under Muslim law (Shufa) — meaning, nature, who can claim; subject matter; formalities and legal effect; legal devices of evading; loss of the right
Pre-emption under Hindu Law

modules.name: Gifts under Muslim Law (Hiba)
modules.description: Nature, characteristics, types, essentials, and revocation of Hiba.
topics: Nature and characteristics of Hiba; types of Hiba; donor and donee; what may be given in gift
Essentials of valid gift; exceptions; oral gift and validity; registration; kinds of gifts; gifts involving return; Marz-ul-mauth (death-bed gift)
Revocation and revival of gift

modules.name: Wakf
modules.description: Origin, development, definition, characteristics, kinds, and administration of Wakf.
topics: Origin and Development of Wakf
Importance, Meaning and Definition, Characteristics
Essentials, Kinds, formalities for creation, the Wakif, Objects and Purposes of the Wakf
Administration of Wakf under the Wakf Act; Appointment, Removal, Powers and Duties of Mutawalli

subjects.name: Penology & Victimology
subjects.description: Definition and scope of Penology, crime control mechanisms (Police, Courts, Prosecutors, Jails, Open Prisons), theories and forms of punishment, and penal policy in India.

modules.name: Penology — Introduction
modules.description: Definition, nature and scope of Penology; overview of Crime Control Mechanism — Police, Court, Public Prosecutor, Jail Administration, Open Prison.
topics: Definition, nature and scope of Penology
Crime Control Mechanism — Police; Court; Public Prosecutor; Jail Administration; Open Prison

modules.name: Punishment
modules.description: Concept of punishment, theories of punishment (Deterrent, Retributive, Preventive, Reformative), forms of punishment, and penal policy in India.
topics: Concept of Punishment
Theories of Punishment — Deterrent Theory; Retributive Theory; Preventive Theory; Reformative Theory
Forms of Punishment
Penal Policy in India

modules.name: Police System in India
modules.description: Origin, development, police force in India, nature and objectives, state/central police organizations, principles of policing, legal functions, law relating to police administration, police reforms, NHRC guidelines.
topics: Origin of Police
Development of Police Organization
Police Force in India
Nature and Objectives of Indian Police System
Police organization under the State Government
Police organization under the Central Government
Principles of Policing
Legal functions of police
Law Relating to Police Administration
Police Reforms; Legislative Trends; Judicial Approaches
NHRC guidelines on Police-Public Relations

modules.name: Prison System in India
modules.description: History of prison system, prison in British India, role in modern penology, types of prisons and prisoners, problems of prisons, and prison reforms.
topics: History of Prison System
Prison in British India
Role of Prison in Modern Penology
Types of Prisons and Prisoners
Problems of Prisons — Over Crowding; Basic Amenities; Prison Discipline; Prisoner's Health; Criminality in Prison; Problems of Under-trials
Prison Reforms — Commission on Prison Reforms; Jurisprudence of Prison Reforms; Legislative Trends; Judicial Trends

modules.name: Open Prisons
modules.description: Definition and origin of Open Prison, the philosophy underlying it, main characteristics, advantages, and critical appreciation of its working.
topics: Definition and Origin of Open Prison
The Philosophy underlying the Open Prison
Main Characteristics of Open Prisons
Advantages of Open Prison
Critical Appreciation of the working of Open Prison

modules.name: Parole
modules.description: Definition and concept of Parole, distinction from indeterminate sentence/furlough/probation, Parole in India, Parole Boards, conditions, essentials of an ideal Parole system, judicial trend, and Parole violation.
topics: Meaning and Definition of Parole
Concept of Parole
Distinction between Parole and Indeterminate Sentence
Distinction between Parole and Furlough
Comparison between Parole and Probation
Parole in India
Structural setup of Parole Boards and their Functions
Conditions of Parole
Essentials of an Ideal Parole System
Judicial Trend in India
Parole Violation

modules.name: Victimology — Victim and Victimization
modules.description: Meaning and kinds of victim, impact of victimization, secondary victimization, definition/nature/scope of victimology, and theories of victimology.
topics: Victim — Meaning and Kinds
Impact of Victimization — Physical, Economic and Psychological
Double / Secondary Victimization
Victimology — Definition, Nature and Scope
Theories of Victimology — The Precipitation Theory; Life-style Theory; Deviant Place Theory; Routine Activity Theory

modules.name: Legal Perspectives of Victim Assistance
modules.description: Victim Assistance Program, victim rights at international and municipal level, UN Declaration, Constitution and statutory provisions; access to justice — compensation, rights during trial, legal assistance, bail, and right to appeal.
topics: Victim Assistance Program — Evolution; Victim's Rights at International and Municipal Jurisdiction; UN Declaration on Victims' Rights; Constitution of India and Rights of Victims; Statutory Provisions — CrPC, Probation of Offenders Act
Access to Justice — Compensation to victims; Rights of victims during trial; Legal assistance; Role of victim at time of granting bail; Right of victim to appeal

subjects.name: Jurisprudence
subjects.description: Introduction to Jurisprudence — meaning, nature, utility, schools of thought, law and morality — and Sources of Law: Custom, Legislation, Precedent, and Juristic Writings.

modules.name: Introduction to Jurisprudence
modules.description: Meaning, nature and utility of jurisprudence; characteristics, purposes and classification of law; and the relationship between law and morality.
topics: Jurisprudence — Meaning, Nature and Utility
Characteristics, Purposes and Classification of Law
Relationship between Law and Morality

modules.name: Sources of Law
modules.description: Custom, Legislation, Precedent (including Doctrine of Stare Decisis, Art.141, ratio decidendi, obiter dicta, prospective overruling), and Juristic Writings.
topics: Custom — Meaning, nature, essential conditions, kinds, concept of Volkgeist
Legislation — Meaning, nature, kinds, merits and demerits, relation with other sources

Precedent — Meaning, nature, theories of Precedent, Doctrine of Stare Decisis, Article 141, kinds, ratio decidendi, obiter dicta, prospective overruling, circumstances destroying binding force, relation with other sources
Juristic Writings — Meaning, nature and significance

modules.name: Natural Law Theories and Revival of Natural Law
modules.description: Classical Natural Law (Plato to Aquinas), Natural Law and Social Contract Theory (Grotius, Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau), and the Revival of Natural Law (Lon Fuller, HLA Hart, John Finnis).
topics: Classical Natural Law theory: Plato to St. Thomas Aquinas
Natural law and Social Contract Theory: Hugo Grotius and International Law, Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau
Revival of Natural Law: Lon Fuller and the Morality of Law; HLA Hart on Natural Law; John Finnis and the Restatement of Natural Law

modules.name: Legal Positivism
modules.description: Bentham and Austin's command theory, HLA Hart's concept of law (Rules of Recognition, Change and Adjudication), and Kelsen's Pure Theory of Law and Grundnorm.
topics: Bentham and John Austin's theory of positivism
Hart's concept of law
Kelsen's Pure Theory of Law

modules.name: Sociological, Realist, Historical Schools and Critical Legal Studies
modules.description: Sociological school (Roscoe Pound), American Realism (Holmes, Llewellyn, Frank), Historical school (Savigny, Maine), and Critical Legal Studies (Feminist Legal Theory, Critical Race Theory).
topics: Sociological school of law — Roscoe Pound
Realist school of law — American Realism: W. Holmes, Karl Llewellyn, Jerome Frank
Historical school of jurisprudence — Savigny and Maine; Comparison of Historical and Analytical School
Critical Legal Studies — (1) Feminist Legal Theory and (2) Critical Race Theory

modules.name: Concept of Person, Right and Duties
modules.description: Nature of personality (natural and legal), kinds of legal persons, theories of legal personality, and the concept of legal rights (Hohfeld's classification, kinds and theories of rights).
topics: Nature of Personality — Natural and Legal; Legal Status of Lower Animals, Dead persons, Unborn Persons; Kinds of Legal Persons; Uses and Purposes of Incorporation; Theories of Legal Personality
Meaning of Wrong, Duty and Right; Characteristics of Legal Rights; Kinds of Legal Rights; Theories of Legal Rights; Hohfeldian Classification of Legal Rights

modules.name: Concepts of Ownership, Possession and Title
modules.description: Meaning, characteristics, kinds and modes of acquiring ownership; meaning, kinds, modes and possessory remedies for possession; and the definition, classification and nature of title.
topics: Meaning of Ownership; Characteristic of Ownership; Subject-matter of Ownership; Kinds of Ownership; Modes of acquiring Ownership
Meaning of Possession; Kinds of Possession; Modes of acquiring Possession; Possessory Remedies; Comparison between Ownership and Possession
Definition and Nature of Title; Classification of Titles; Importance of Agreements; Kinds of Agreements; Validity of Agreement

modules.name: Obligations and Liability
modules.description: Definition, sources and kinds of obligation; nature, kinds and conditions of liability; strict and absolute liability; vicarious liability in civil and criminal law; and liability of corporations.
topics: Definition of Obligation; Solitary Obligations; Sources of Obligations

Nature of Liability; Kinds of Liability; General Conditions of Liability; Measure of Penal Liability; Measure of Civil Liability; Theory of Strict and Absolute Liability; Vicarious Liability in Civil and Criminal Law; Liability of Corporations

subjects.name: Media Law
subjects.description: Introduction to media and communication, historical foundations of media laws in UK/USA/India, international law and freedom of media, six theories of the press, and statutory regulatory framework.

modules.name: Introduction
modules.description: Introduction to media and communication, importance of media in democracy, kinds of media, and functions of media.
topics: Introduction to Media and Communication
Importance of Media in Democracy
Kinds of Media
Functions of Media — Information, Surveillance, Service the economic system, hold society together, Entertain, Act as a community forum, Service the political system

modules.name: History of Press and Theories of Press
modules.description: Historical foundations of media laws in UK, USA and India (pre and post-independence), international law and freedom of media, and the six theories of press.
topics: Historical Foundations of Media Laws in UK, USA and India (Pre and Post-Independence)
International Law and Freedom of Media (UDHR, ICCPR, ECOSOC etc.)
Theories of Press — Authoritarian Theory; Libertarian Theory; Communist Theory; Theory of Social Responsibility; Development Media Theory; Democratic Participant Media Theory

modules.name: Constitutional Framework of Freedom of Media in India
modules.description: Free speech and constituent assembly debates, facets of freedom of speech and expression (Art. 19), Law Commission 101st Report, reasonable restrictions, legislative privileges, privacy and media.
topics: Free Speech and Constituent Assembly Debates in India
Freedom of Speech and Expression in Indian Constitution
Facets of Freedom of Speech and Expression: Freedom of Press; Right to Circulation; Right to Receive Information; Right to Advertise; Right to Telecast/Broadcast; Censorship
Law Commission of India: 101st Report on Freedom of Speech and Expression under Article 19 — Overview
Reasonable Restrictions
Legislative Privileges and Media
Right to Privacy and Media
Freedom of Media during emergency

modules.name: Legal Dimensions of Media
modules.description: Media and criminal law (sedition, obscenity, defamation), law of torts (defamation, negligence), contempt of court, RTI/Official Secrets Act, and Working Journalists Act.
topics: Media and Criminal Law (Sedition, Obscenity and Defamation)
Media and Law of Torts (Civil Law of Defamation and Negligence)
Media and Judiciary (Contempt of Court)
Media and Executive — Overview (The Official Secrets Act 1923, The Right to Information Act 2005)
Media and Journalists — Overview (The Working Journalists (Conditions of Service) Act 1955)

modules.name: Regulatory Framework of Media
modules.description: Methods of regulation, Cinematograph Act, Cable TV Networks Act, Prasar Bharati Act, Press Council Act, TRAI Act, ASCI codes, Indecent Representation of Women Act, and free speech and fair trial.
topics: Methods of Regulation (Self-Regulation and Statutory Regulation)
The Cinematograph Act, 1952
The Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995
The Prasar Bharati Act, 1990
The Press Council of India Act, 1978
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997
Advertising Standards Council of India and its codes
The Indecent Representation of Women Act, 1986

Free Speech and Fair Trial; Sting Operations; Broadcasting Rights; Media and Convergence; Infringement of IPR; Internet and freedom of media; Violence against Media persons; Role of media in electoral process

semesters.name: Semester 3
semesters.description: Second year studies focusing on specialized legal areas and advanced constitutional principles.

semesters.name: Semester 4
semesters.description: Continuing second year legal education with focus on procedural aspects and specialized subjects.

semesters.name: Semester 5
semesters.description: Third year studies with advanced electives and professional legal skills.

semesters.name: Semester 6
